text:
- chief complaint: uncontrolled hypertension despite medication, referred by new PCP for elevated blood pressure and possible kidney concerns noted on recent blood work.
- history of present illness: the patient started seeing a new PCP last year, who adjusted medications for high blood pressure; home readings have risen (up to 170/90), and the PCP increased medications again. The patient reports adherence, but control remains difficult. Family history includes hypertension in both parents and kidney disease in one parent.
- physical examination: BP 169/74, HR 88, SpO2 98%. No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits. Lungs clear. Heart with a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. 1+ bilateral pitting edema.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: mild headaches with high blood pressure; intermittent ankle swelling after prolonged standing; no chest pain or shortness of breath, even with exertion.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: cardura (doxazosin) 4 mg once daily; stop nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (advil, motrin, aleve); use tylenol for pain.
- follow-up instructions: renal artery ultrasound, repeat urine collection, morning aldosterone and renin levels, 24-hour urine test; reduce alcohol to 1–2 drinks per week; reduce salt intake; nutritionist referral; record home blood pressures at the same time daily and return in 3 weeks; doctor will coordinate with PCP.
